name: Pale black shade
lede: Pale black shade is a near-black plum, filed under a traditional Japanese name, Sensaicha, "thousand year old brown," whose own origin is undocumented.

sections.title: A brown with no history given
sections.body:
Our library lists this swatch as *Sensaicha* (千歳茶), which translates as "thousand year old brown," grouped with the traditional colors of Japan [1]. Unlike most of that family, our data gives this one's own tier as undocumented: no plant, era or dyer is attached to the name in the sources checked here, only the translation itself [1]. The library also carries an alternate hex, #3B3429, for the same name, a reminder that traditional-color swatches vary by source [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[vivid-black]], only 2.9 units off, essentially the same color on screen [2]; [[continental-blue]] sits 3.4 units away. It shares its graph hex exactly with the separately named [[pale-black-shade]] (Shikon, blue-violet) [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 618 of 23,781 paintings, 2.6 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 518 [3]. It most often plays a shadow, in 46 percent of those 518 paintings by lightness rank, so varnish cannot fake the result [3]. The earliest match dates to the year 1201, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3]. A name meaning "a thousand years old" naturally outruns any dated painting in our archive; the phrase describes a shade of aged brown, not a literal age.
